items.stem: Which type of plate boundary is the San Andreas Fault in California?
items.answer: Transform (conservative)
items.markingKey: B. The Pacific and North American plates slide past each other.

items.stem: Mateo writes: "The Richter scale goes up evenly, so a magnitude 8 is twice as strong as a magnitude 4." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Magnitude scales are logarithmic: each whole number means about 10 times more shaking and about 32 times more energy.
items.markingKey: Magnitude scales are logarithmic: each whole number means about 10 times more shaking and about 32 times more energy. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between a convergent boundary and a divergent boundary.
items.answer: At a divergent boundary plates move apart and new crust forms; at a convergent boundary plates move together and crust is destroyed by subduction or crumpled into mountains.
items.markingKey: At a divergent boundary plates move apart and new crust forms; at a convergent boundary plates move together and crust is destroyed by subduction or crumpled into mountains. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Formulate an action plan to investigate the research question "Why did the 2010 Chile earthquake (magnitude 8.8) cause far fewer deaths than the 2010 Haiti earthquake (magnitude 7.0)?" Include the main steps, at least one primary and one secondary source, and how you would record your findings.
items.answer: Collect USGS data on magnitude, depth and distance; collect death tolls and GDP per capita from UN/World Bank; research building codes in both countries; compare in a table; evaluate source reliability.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Collect USGS data on magnitude, depth and distance; collect death tolls and GDP per capita from UN/World Bank; research building codes in both countries; compare in a table; evaluate source reliability. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.answer: It links plate tectonics to the global context of fairness and development and uses comparable, well-documented events.

items.stem: The 2023 Türkiye–Syria earthquake had a moment magnitude of 7.8; the 2017 Puebla earthquake, Mexico had a magnitude of 7.1. Each whole step on the magnitude scale means about 10 times more ground shaking (amplitude) and about 32 times more energy. Calculate how many times greater (a) the amplitude and (b) the energy release of the larger earthquake was.
items.answer: (a) about 5 times; (b) about 11 times
items.markingKey: Difference 0.7 (M1); amplitude 10^0.7 ≈ 5 (A1); energy 10^(1.5×0.7) ≈ 11 (A1; 32^0.7 accepted). Magnitude does not on its own decide the death toll – vulnerability does.

items.stem:
Source A – Scientific agency summary (paraphrased): Summary of United States Geological Survey (USGS) information on the 2015 Nepal earthquake

The Indian Plate is moving north-north-east into the Eurasian Plate at about 4 to 5 cm per year. This collision has built the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau. The 2015 Gorkha earthquake was caused by sudden slip on the main thrust fault beneath Nepal.

How reliable is Source A for someone researching plate tectonics, earthquakes and volcanoes? Justify your answer using its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Summary of United States Geological Survey (USGS) information on the 2015 Nepal earthquake. Purpose: to explain the scientific causes of the earthquake to the public. Value: USGS is a leading scientific agency, so the data on plate movement and the cause of the earthquake are reliable. Limitation: It explains the physical cause but says little about why so many people died (building quality, poverty, access).
items.markingKey: Origin: Summary of United States Geological Survey (USGS) information on the 2015 Nepal earthquake. Purpose: to explain the scientific causes of the earthquake to the public. Value: USGS is a leading scientific agency, so the data on plate movement and the cause of the earthquake are reliable. Limitation: It explains the physical cause but says little about why so many people died (building quality, poverty, access). Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Earthquakes are more dangerous than volcanoes."
items.answer: Thesis: Generally true for loss of life because earthquakes cannot be predicted, but the danger of either depends on the size of the event and the vulnerability of the people affected.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: earthquakes strike with almost no warning; they have caused most of the deadliest disasters, e.g. Haiti 2010 and the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. Counter-arguments: volcanoes can be deadly and affect the whole world, such as Tambora in 1815; ash clouds, lahars and gases have long-lasting impacts. Thesis/conclusion: Generally true for loss of life because earthquakes cannot be predicted, but the danger of either depends on the size of the event and the vulnerability of the people affected. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Briefly explain why tectonic plates move.
items.answer: Heat from the Earth's core drives convection in the mantle; ridge push at spreading ridges and slab pull at subduction zones move the plates a few centimetres a year.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Heat from the Earth's core drives convection in the mantle; ridge push at spreading ridges and slab pull at subduction zones move the plates a few centimetres a year. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between the focus and the epicentre.
items.answer: The focus is the point underground where the earthquake starts; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it.
items.markingKey: The focus is the point underground where the earthquake starts; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Yusuf argues that "Earthquakes are more dangerous than volcanoes." Lukas disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: Generally true for loss of life because earthquakes cannot be predicted, but the danger of either depends on the size of the event and the vulnerability of the people affected.
items.markingKey: Yusuf: earthquakes strike with almost no warning. Lukas: volcanoes can be deadly and affect the whole world, such as Tambora in 1815. Judgement (1-2 marks): Generally true for loss of life because earthquakes cannot be predicted, but the danger of either depends on the size of the event and the vulnerability of the people affected.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The effect of distance from the sea on climate: inland places have hotter summers and colder winters"?
items.answer: continentality
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of continentality.

items.stem: Explain why mountains often have more rainfall on one side than the other.
items.answer: Moist air rises on the windward side, cools and condenses, giving relief rain; air descending on the leeward side warms and dries, creating a rain shadow.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Moist air rises on the windward side, cools and condenses, giving relief rain; air descending on the leeward side warms and dries, creating a rain shadow. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between convectional rainfall and relief rainfall.
items.answer: Relief rain forms when air is forced up over mountains; convectional rain forms when the ground heats air so it rises, typically in afternoon thunderstorms in hot places.
items.markingKey: Relief rain forms when air is forced up over mountains; convectional rain forms when the ground heats air so it rises, typically in afternoon thunderstorms in hot places. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "How does the microclimate (temperature and wind speed) vary between five locations around our school grounds?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.
items.answer: Choose five sites (car park, field, courtyard, under trees, near buildings); measure temperature and wind speed at the same times on three days; record; draw a map with proportional symbols; explain differences; evaluate instrument accuracy.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Choose five sites (car park, field, courtyard, under trees, near buildings); measure temperature and wind speed at the same times on three days; record; draw a map with proportional symbols; explain differences; evaluate instrument accuracy. items.stem:
Study the climate data for Reykjavik (Iceland):
Month: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
Temp (°C): 0 0 1 3 7 10 12 11 8 4 1 0
Rain (mm): 76 72 82 58 44 50 52 62 67 86 73 79
Identify the wettest month and state its rainfall.
items.answer: October, 86 mm
items.markingKey: October (86 mm).

items.stem:
Source A – Meteorological office information (paraphrased): Summary of guidance from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)

Climate averages, or "normals", are calculated over a 30-year period so that unusual years do not distort the picture. The current standard period is 1991–2020. Because the climate is changing, normals are updated every ten years.

How reliable is Source A for someone researching weather, climate and climate graphs? Justify your answer using its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Summary of guidance from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). Purpose: to explain to the public and national weather services how climate averages are defined. Value: It is the official international body for meteorology, so the definition is authoritative. Limitation: It explains the method but does not show how much climate has changed between periods.
items.markingKey: Origin: Summary of guidance from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). Purpose: to explain to the public and national weather services how climate averages are defined. Value: It is the official international body for meteorology, so the definition is authoritative. Limitation: It explains the method but does not show how much climate has changed between periods. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". items.stem: Air temperature generally falls with height by about…
items.markingKey: C. This is the average environmental lapse rate.

items.stem: Using the Western Ghats and the Deccan Plateau, India as an example, explain relief rainfall and rain shadow.
items.answer: Monsoon winds bring over 2 500 mm of rain a year to the windward western slopes, while places on the plateau to the east receive much less. Mountains force air to rise and lose moisture on one side, leaving the other side drier.
items.markingKey: Context (Monsoon winds bring over 2 500 mm of rain a year to the windward western slopes, while places on the plateau to the east receive much less.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: mountains force air to rise and lose moisture on one side, leaving the other side drier. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to relief rainfall and rain shadow.

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Latitude is the most important factor affecting climate."
items.answer: Thesis: Largely true at the global scale, but at regional and local scales altitude, continentality and ocean currents can matter more.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: it controls the angle and amount of solar energy, setting the main climate zones; it explains the pattern from equatorial to polar climates. Counter-arguments: altitude makes places like Nairobi mild despite being near the equator; ocean currents and distance from the sea cause big differences at the same latitude. Thesis/conclusion: Largely true at the global scale, but at regional and local scales altitude, continentality and ocean currents can matter more. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "Saffir–Simpson scale".
items.answer: A 1–5 scale that classifies hurricanes by their maximum sustained wind speed

items.stem: Distinguish between a drought and a flash flood.
items.answer: A flash flood is a sudden excess of water after intense rain; a drought is a long-lasting shortage of water caused by lack of precipitation.
items.markingKey: A flash flood is a sudden excess of water after intense rain; a drought is a long-lasting shortage of water caused by lack of precipitation. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why storm surges often cause more deaths than the winds of a tropical cyclone.
items.answer: Low pressure and strong onshore winds raise the sea several metres and push it inland quickly over low-lying coasts, drowning people and destroying homes. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)

Source A – Humanitarian report (paraphrased): Summary of UN OCHA and Philippine government reports on Typhoon Haiyan, 2013–2014

After Typhoon Haiyan struck the central Philippines, about 14 million people were affected and around 1 million homes were damaged or destroyed. Many deaths in Tacloban were caused by the storm surge rather than by the wind, as some residents did not understand the warning term "storm surge".

What is the message of Source A about tropical storms, floods and droughts? Refer to details in the source.
items.answer: Haiyan affected millions, and many deaths came from a storm surge that people did not understand.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "Droughts are a more serious hazard than tropical storms."
items.answer: In terms of the number of people affected over time, droughts are often more serious, but tropical storms cause more sudden loss of life and damage; severity depends on vulnerability.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: droughts affect larger areas and more people over longer periods; they cause famine, migration and conflict. Arguments against: tropical storms cause sudden, concentrated death and destruction; storms damage infrastructure and economies very quickly. Supported judgement: In terms of the number of people affected over time, droughts are often more serious, but tropical storms cause more sudden loss of life and damage; severity depends on vulnerability.

Before Cyclone Amphan reached the coast in May 2020, Bangladesh's government and volunteers moved about 2.4 million people into shelters, including thousands of extra shelters opened to allow social distancing during the COVID-19 pandemic. Deaths in Bangladesh were reported in the dozens rather than the thousands.

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Preparation is more important than prediction in reducing deaths from natural hazards."
items.answer: Thesis: Largely agree: prediction is useless without preparation, and preparation also works for unpredictable hazards; but for storms and eruptions the two are linked.

items.stem: Distinguish between a divergent boundary and a convergent boundary.
items.answer: At a divergent boundary plates move apart and new crust forms; at a convergent boundary plates move together and crust is destroyed by subduction or crumpled into mountains.
items.markingKey: At a divergent boundary plates move apart and new crust forms; at a convergent boundary plates move together and crust is destroyed by subduction or crumpled into mountains. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Using the 2010 earthquakes in Haiti and Chile as an example, explain vulnerability and development.
items.answer: Haiti's magnitude 7.0 earthquake killed well over 100 000 people; Chile's magnitude 8.8 earthquake six weeks later killed about 525. Chile's building codes, wealth and preparation reduced deaths despite a far stronger earthquake.
items.markingKey: Context (Haiti's magnitude 7.0 earthquake killed well over 100 000 people; Chile's magnitude 8.8 earthquake six weeks later killed about 525.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Chile's building codes, wealth and preparation reduced deaths despite a far stronger earthquake. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to vulnerability and development.

items.stem: Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why mountains often have more rainfall on one side than the other.
items.answer: Moist air rises on the windward side, cools and condenses, giving relief rain; air descending on the leeward side warms and dries, creating a rain shadow.
items.markingKey: Content: Moist air rises on the windward side, cools and condenses, giving relief rain; air descending on the leeward side warms and dries, creating a rain shadow. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why tropical cyclones form only between about 5° and 30° from the equator.
items.answer: They need warm oceans of at least 26.5 °C, found in the tropics, and the Coriolis effect to make the storm spin – which is too weak within about 5° of the equator.
items.markingKey: Content: They need warm oceans of at least 26.5 °C, found in the tropics, and the Coriolis effect to make the storm spin – which is too weak within about 5° of the equator. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. items.stem: Using accurate subject terminology and at least one specific example, write a structured paragraph that responds to: Explain why Iceland has many volcanoes.
items.answer: It sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a divergent boundary, and above a hotspot, so magma rises easily to the surface.
items.markingKey: Content: It sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a divergent boundary, and above a hotspot, so magma rises easily to the surface. items.stem: Reported disaster events worldwide per decade was 1,600 events in 1980 and 3,700 events in 2010 (approx., EM-DAT). Calculate the percentage change.
items.markingKey: Percentage change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100 (M1) = (3,700 − 1,600) ÷ 1,600 × 100 = +131.2% (A1). Dividing by the new value is a common error.

items.stem: Justify the relevance of the research question "How does the microclimate (temperature and wind speed) vary between five locations around our school grounds?"
items.answer: It applies weather measurement skills to a local scale and can be collected safely and repeated.
items.markingKey: It applies weather measurement skills to a local scale and can be collected safely and repeated. items.stem:
Source A – Humanitarian report (paraphrased): Summary of UN OCHA and Philippine government reports on Typhoon Haiyan, 2013–2014

After Typhoon Haiyan struck the central Philippines, about 14 million people were affected and around 1 million homes were damaged or destroyed. Many deaths in Tacloban were caused by the storm surge rather than by the wind, as some residents did not understand the warning term "storm surge".

How reliable is Source A for someone researching tropical storms, floods and droughts? Justify your answer using its origin and purpose.
items.answer: Origin: Summary of UN OCHA and Philippine government reports on Typhoon Haiyan, 2013–2014. Purpose: to report the scale of the disaster and lessons for future warnings. Value: It is based on official data and highlights a key lesson about how warnings are communicated. Limitation: Death and damage figures were estimates made during the crisis, and the report does not give the perspective of survivors directly.
items.markingKey: Origin: Summary of UN OCHA and Philippine government reports on Typhoon Haiyan, 2013–2014. Purpose: to report the scale of the disaster and lessons for future warnings. Value: It is based on official data and highlights a key lesson about how warnings are communicated. Limitation: Death and damage figures were estimates made during the crisis, and the report does not give the perspective of survivors directly. Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". MYP I&S criterion D (year 3), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly analyses concepts and issues, summarises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose recognising value and limitations, and clearly recognises different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem:
Source A – Scientific agency summary (paraphrased): Summary of United States Geological Survey (USGS) information on the 2015 Nepal earthquake

The Indian Plate is moving north-north-east into the Eurasian Plate at about 4 to 5 cm per year. This collision has built the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau. The 2015 Gorkha earthquake was caused by sudden slip on the main thrust fault beneath Nepal.

"Earthquakes are more dangerous than volcanoes." Using Source A and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree?
items.answer: Generally true for loss of life because earthquakes cannot be predicted, but the danger of either depends on the size of the event and the vulnerability of the people affected.
items.markingKey: From the source: The earthquake was caused by the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates. Own knowledge for: earthquakes strike with almost no warning; they have caused most of the deadliest disasters, e.g. Haiti 2010 and the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. Own knowledge against: volcanoes can be deadly and affect the whole world, such as Tambora in 1815; ash clouds, lahars and gases have long-lasting impacts. Judgement: Generally true for loss of life because earthquakes cannot be predicted, but the danger of either depends on the size of the event and the vulnerability of the people affected. Top answers integrate the source with own knowledge and comment on the source's origin/purpose. MYP I&S criterion D (year 3), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly analyses concepts and issues, summarises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose recognising value and limitations, and clearly recognises different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem:
Source A – News report (paraphrased): Summary of reports by Reuters and the Bangladesh Ministry of Disaster Management, May 2020

Before Cyclone Amphan reached the coast in May 2020, Bangladesh's government and volunteers moved about 2.4 million people into shelters, including thousands of extra shelters opened to allow social distancing during the COVID-19 pandemic. Deaths in Bangladesh were reported in the dozens rather than the thousands.

Using Source A and your own knowledge, evaluate the claim that "Preparation is more important than prediction in reducing deaths from natural hazards."
items.answer: Largely agree: prediction is useless without preparation, and preparation also works for unpredictable hazards; but for storms and eruptions the two are linked.
items.markingKey: From the source: A huge, organised evacuation kept deaths in Bangladesh low during Cyclone Amphan. Own knowledge for: preparation (drills, building codes, shelters) protects people even when hazards cannot be predicted, e.g. earthquakes; Bangladesh shows preparation saves lives. Own knowledge against: without forecasts, evacuation for cyclones and eruptions would be impossible; prediction and preparation work best together. Judgement: Largely agree: prediction is useless without preparation, and preparation also works for unpredictable hazards; but for storms and eruptions the two are linked. Top answers integrate the source with own knowledge and comment on the source's origin/purpose. MYP I&S criterion D (year 3), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly analyses concepts and issues, summarises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose recognising value and limitations, and clearly recognises different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem:
Source A – Meteorological office information (paraphrased): Summary of guidance from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)

Climate averages, or "normals", are calculated over a 30-year period so that unusual years do not distort the picture. The current standard period is 1991–2020. Because the climate is changing, normals are updated every ten years.

"Latitude is the most important factor affecting climate." Using Source A and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree?
items.answer: Largely true at the global scale, but at regional and local scales altitude, continentality and ocean currents can matter more.
items.markingKey: From the source: Climate is measured using 30-year averages, updated every decade. Own knowledge for: it controls the angle and amount of solar energy, setting the main climate zones; it explains the pattern from equatorial to polar climates. Own knowledge against: altitude makes places like Nairobi mild despite being near the equator; ocean currents and distance from the sea cause big differences at the same latitude. Judgement: Largely true at the global scale, but at regional and local scales altitude, continentality and ocean currents can matter more. Top answers integrate the source with own knowledge and comment on the source's origin/purpose. MYP I&S criterion D (year 3), scaled to the marks: 7-8 thoroughly analyses concepts and issues, summarises information to make valid, well-supported arguments, analyses a range of sources in terms of origin and purpose recognising value and limitations, and clearly recognises different perspectives and their implications; 5-6 substantial; 3-4 adequate, partly descriptive; 1-2 limited, mostly assertion.

items.stem: A class brainstorm on tropical storms, floods and droughts produced the question "Why are storms dangerous?" Explain why it needs refining, then suggest an improved research question and justify your change.
items.answer: Weakness: it is too broad and general, with no named event or measurable outcome Improved: "To what extent did early warnings reduce deaths from Cyclone Fani in Odisha, India, in 2019?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is too broad and general, with no named event or measurable outcome); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "To what extent did early warnings reduce deaths from Cyclone Fani in Odisha, India, in 2019?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "magma"?
options: The effect of distance from the sea on climate: inland places have hotter summers and colder winters
The amount of water vapour in the air
The ability of a community to cope with and recover from a hazard
Molten rock beneath the Earth's surface; it is called lava when it erupts
items.answer: Molten rock beneath the Earth's surface; it is called lava when it erupts
items.markingKey: D. "magma" is molten rock beneath the Earth's surface; it is called lava when it erupts.

items.stem: Bangladesh has built thousands of what to protect people from cyclones?
items.answer: Raised cyclone shelters
items.markingKey: D. They also serve as schools.

items.stem: Which of these places has the largest annual temperature range?
items.answer: Moscow, Russia
items.markingKey: Moscow, Russia. Continental interiors have the greatest range.

items.stem: A student claims: "Droughts happen suddenly, like floods." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Droughts develop slowly over months or years and are often called "creeping" hazards.
items.markingKey: Droughts develop slowly over months or years and are often called "creeping" hazards. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Lars writes: "Plates move very quickly during an earthquake and drift several metres every year." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Plates move only a few centimetres a year on average; earthquakes release years of built-up strain in seconds.
items.markingKey: Plates move only a few centimetres a year on average; earthquakes release years of built-up strain in seconds. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "Rich countries do not suffer from natural disasters." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: They do – e.g. Hurricane Katrina (2005) in the USA – but they usually have fewer deaths and higher economic losses because of better protection and more valuable property.
items.markingKey: They do – e.g. Hurricane Katrina (2005) in the USA – but they usually have fewer deaths and higher economic losses because of better protection and more valuable property. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Distinguish between convectional rainfall and relief rainfall.
items.answer: Relief rain forms when air is forced up over mountains; convectional rain forms when the ground heats air so it rises, typically in afternoon thunderstorms in hot places.
items.markingKey: Relief rain forms when air is forced up over mountains; convectional rain forms when the ground heats air so it rises, typically in afternoon thunderstorms in hot places. items.stem: Explain why storm surges often cause more deaths than the winds of a tropical cyclone.
items.answer: Low pressure and strong onshore winds raise the sea several metres and push it inland quickly over low-lying coasts, drowning people and destroying homes.

items.stem: Plan an extended response to the question: "Droughts are a more serious hazard than tropical storms." To what extent do you agree? Give a thesis, two arguments with specific evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion.
items.answer: Thesis: In terms of the number of people affected over time, droughts are often more serious, but tropical storms cause more sudden loss of life and damage; severity depends on vulnerability.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: droughts affect larger areas and more people over longer periods; they cause famine, migration and conflict. Counter-arguments: tropical storms cause sudden, concentrated death and destruction; storms damage infrastructure and economies very quickly. Thesis/conclusion: In terms of the number of people affected over time, droughts are often more serious, but tropical storms cause more sudden loss of life and damage; severity depends on vulnerability. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).
